title: BHU students march to demand restoration of elected union in Varanasi
seoTitle: Varanasi march for BHU students union

tea.why: BHU students have not had an elected students' union for nearly thirty years, limiting campus representation.
tea.want: Students demand a time-bound election schedule for a restored students' union following Lyngdoh Committee rules.
tea.changed: Oct 28: Student groups held a 'March for Democracy' across the BHU campus to demand union elections.

summary: Student groups at Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi staged a 'March for Democracy' on October 28, 2026, demanding the revival of an elected students' union. Organised jointly by the National Students' Union of India, All India Students' Association, Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, and DISHA, the rally marched from Vishwanath Temple to the Students' Union Building. Protesters highlighted that BHU has lacked an elected union since 1997. Aside from restoring elections under Lyngdoh Committee recommendations, students raised concerns regarding campus Wi-Fi, library hours, and hostel security for women. No official response from university authorities was detailed in reported sources.
demands: Restore the elected BHU students' union
Set a time-bound schedule for union elections
Follow Lyngdoh Committee guidelines for elections
Improve campus facilities including Wi-Fi and library hours
Enhance security arrangements at women's hostels
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Student organisations submitted a memorandum to the Dean of Students calling for union elections and campus facility improvements.
BHU student groups held the 'March for Democracy' from Vishwanath Temple to the Students' Union Building.
